governing_constraint.rule: Educate everyone; enfranchise by law — not by examination.

hypothesis.text: Under identifiable institutional conditions — especially local decision-making, civic education, and dense civic networks — extending suffrage to 16- and 17-year-olds for local elections may strengthen meaningful and durable civic participation without requiring civic tests, certifications, academic achievement, service hours, or political-knowledge prerequisites for the franchise.
hypothesis.central_question: Under what institutional conditions does enfranchisement at 16 produce meaningful, durable civic participation?
hypothesis.constitutional_capitalism_test: Can local suffrage at 16 deepen self-government by connecting young citizens to institutions that already govern their lives, without converting civic preparation into a franchise gate and without assuming that rights alone repair a low-participation civic culture?

governance.reason: Steve-directed upgrade from speculative card to serious comparative empirical track. Maryland municipal experiments, Newark low-turnout school-board case, Brattleboro, and international cases now justify structured falsification. Not a principle. Not locked policy.

four_propositions.name: capability
four_propositions.question: Do 16–17-year-olds make meaningfully lower-quality political choices than older voters?
four_propositions.initial_signal: Austrian peer-reviewed evidence does not support treating inferior capability as established fact; does not automatically establish the CC hypothesis.
four_propositions.verdict_slot: Supports | Qualifies | Contradicts | Not Enough Evidence

four_propositions.name: participation
four_propositions.question: Do 16–17-year-olds register and vote when eligible, relative to overall electorate and young-adult cohorts?
four_propositions.initial_signal: Newark: 1,851 registered / 73 voted (~3.94%) vs overall turnout ~3.47% — youth slightly above a collapsed electorate, not proof that '16-year-olds don't vote.'
four_propositions.verdict_slot: Supports | Qualifies | Contradicts | Not Enough Evidence

four_propositions.name: habit_formation
four_propositions.question: Does voting at 16–17, while embedded in schools/families/communities, raise later habitual adult participation?
four_propositions.verdict_slot: Supports | Qualifies | Contradicts | Not Enough Evidence

four_propositions.name: system_effects
four_propositions.question: Does enfranchisement change schools, campaigns, journalism, families, candidate behavior, or local government responsiveness?
four_propositions.initial_signal: Not Enough Evidence at registration; requires case measurement.
four_propositions.verdict_slot: Supports | Qualifies | Contradicts | Not Enough Evidence

sequencing_test.prior_design_preference: build excellent universal civic education first → then extend local suffrage to 16
sequencing_test.explicit_research_question: Should civic education precede youth enfranchisement, or does enfranchisement itself make civic education more effective?
sequencing_test.rule: Reality answers — not initial design preference.

hard_distinctions.rule: Extending suffrage ≠ repairing a civic culture in which almost nobody participates.
hard_distinctions.target: Newark as failure-mode/control case; converges with HYP-126

hard_distinctions.rule: Local suffrage experiment ≠ automatic federal/statewide age change.
hard_distinctions.target: Maryland municipal model is the primary U.S. laboratory

hard_distinctions.rule: Aggregate turnout rise after youth enfranchisement ≠ youth voting caused the rise.

hard_distinctions.target: No new principle under architecture freeze

institutional_conditions_matrix.question: Under what institutional conditions does enfranchisement at 16 produce meaningful, durable civic participation?

Later Maryland adopter; 2019 first election with 16+ eligible

case_set.place: Other Maryland municipalities with youth voting
case_set.why: Same-state comparative opportunities under broadly similar state conditions

case_set.why: Same community/young population; eligibility differs by institution/ballot
Failure-mode/control: 1,851 registered / 73 voted (~3.94%) vs overall ~3.47% turnout — rights without repaired civic culture
2014 independence referendum experience and subsequent elections
2021 + 2026 cycles; aggregate turnout rose 46.6%→51.6% — study covariates, do not claim youth voting caused the rise

quasi_experimental_design_md.structure: municipality before reform → after reform → neighboring municipality without reform → later-adopting municipality
quasi_experimental_design_md.requirement: Underlying election records sufficiently detailed for age/cohort measurement
quasi_experimental_design_md.note: Maryland is the primary U.S. laboratory because multiple municipal experiments share broadly similar state conditions without statewide/federal 16+ suffrage.

distributed_civic_commons.rule: Voting rights + civic education + civic networks + meaningful local institutions may need to be studied together.

journalism.rule: Local-news coverage of youth-relevant contests is part of the measurement bundle and institutional-conditions matrix.

citizenship_framework.rule: Universal civic preparation remains an obligation; it never becomes a ballot gate.

civic_engagement_community_structure.rule: Adult civic-structure baselines (turnout stability × ownership/media/institutions) are control context before attributing youth-suffrage outcomes to voting age alone.
